# Compare two product specs with Copilot

You've got two product pages open and need to decide which one fits your needs. Instead of reading both from top to bottom, give Copilot the key specs and let it list the differences for you. In minutes, you'll have a clear side-by-side summary—no PhD in spreadsheets required.

## Before you start
- A **GitHub account** (free is fine)
- A **computer or phone** with a web browser
- Two product pages open in separate tabs (for example, two software pricing pages or two laptop spec sheets)
- Rough time needed: **5 minutes**

---

## Step 1 — Open Copilot in your browser
Go to [github.com/github-copilot](https://github.com/github-copilot) and sign in with your GitHub account. Alternatively, you can find Copilot through the GitHub homepage by clicking the Copilot option in the navigation menu. You'll see a chat box ready for your question.

If you already use Copilot in another way (like in your IDE or on Windows), you can also access the web-based chat from the main GitHub interface.

💬 Example:
Type or paste:
"Hello"

You'll know it worked when Copilot replies with something like "Hi there! How can I help you today?"

---

## Step 2 — Share the first product's specs
Since Copilot can't automatically read external web pages, you'll need to copy the key specs from the product page yourself. Go to your first product page, select and copy the main specifications (like processor, RAM, storage, screen size, weight, and price), then paste them into the chat box.

💬 Example:
Paste:
"Here are the specs for the first laptop: Processor: Intel Core i7-13700H, RAM: 16GB LPDDR5, Storage: 1TB SSD, Screen: 14\" 2.8K OLED 120Hz, Weight: 1.4kg, Price: $2,199"

You'll know it worked when Copilot acknowledges the specs and confirms it's ready to compare.

---

## Step 3 — Ask Copilot to format the specs
Now, tell Copilot how you want the specs organized. Type:
"Format these specs as a clean bullet-point list."

Copilot will return a neat list of the specs you shared, making them easy to compare with the second product.

💬 Example:
Type:
"Format these specs as a clean bullet-point list."

You'll know it worked when you see a clear list like:
• Processor: Intel Core i7-13700H
• RAM: 16GB LPDDR5
• Storage: 1TB SSD
• Screen: 14" 2.8K OLED 120Hz
• Weight: 1.4kg
• Price: $2,199

---

## Step 4 — Repeat for the second product
Go back to your browser and copy the key specs from the second product page. Return to Copilot and paste those specs into the chat.

💬 Example:
Paste:
"Now for the second laptop: Processor: AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS, RAM: 32GB LPDDR5, Storage: 512GB SSD, Screen: 16\" 2.5K IPS 165Hz, Weight: 1.8kg, Price: $1,799"

You'll know it worked when Copilot acknowledges the second set of specs.

---

## Step 5 — Ask Copilot to compare the two lists
Now ask Copilot to compare the two sets of specs. Type:
"Compare these two products and list the differences in a clear table or bullet list."

Copilot will take the two lists and highlight what's different—like RAM upgrades, storage options, screen refresh rates, or price changes.

💬 Example:
Type:
"Compare these two products and list the differences in a clear table or bullet list."

You'll know it worked when you see a concise comparison like:
• RAM: 16GB vs 32GB (second product has more)
• Storage: 1TB vs 512GB (first product has more)
• Price: $2,199 vs $1,799 (second product is cheaper)
• Screen: 14" vs 16" (second product has a larger screen)

---

## Step 6 — Ask for a recommendation (optional)
If you're still unsure, ask Copilot to give a simple recommendation based on your needs. Type:
"Which of these two products is better for video editing on a budget?"

Copilot will weigh the specs against your stated use case and suggest the better option.

💬 Example:
Type:
"Which of these two products is better for video editing on a budget?"

You'll know it worked when Copilot gives a concise recommendation with reasons.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting the wrong specs**: Double-check what you're copying from the product page. If you include the wrong specs, just paste the correct information and ask Copilot to start over.
- **Not including enough detail**: If you only paste partial specs, Copilot can't give you a full comparison. Include the key specs: processor, RAM, storage, screen, weight, and price.
- **Assuming Copilot remembers**: Copilot doesn't keep memory between chats. If you open a new chat, you'll need to paste both sets of specs again. Bookmark your chat or keep it open to avoid redoing steps.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: Next time you're choosing between two gadgets, appliances, or software tools, use Copilot to do the heavy lifting. Copy the specs, paste them in, and get a clear comparison in seconds—no more squinting at tiny font on a phone screen.
- **For your business or work**: When your team debates which tool to adopt, run this comparison in a shared chat. Everyone sees the same facts, and you avoid long email threads full of conflicting opinions.
- **If you're just getting started**: Start with two simple product pages you already have open. Try the steps above, and you'll see how easy it is to turn messy specs into a clean comparison.

---

## Try it now
Open two product pages in your browser right now. Copy the first set of specs, go to [github.com/github-copilot](https://github.com/github-copilot), paste them in, and ask Copilot to format them. Do the same for the second page, then ask it to compare them. You'll have your answer in under five minutes—no spreadsheets, no PhD required.
